pages.title: Resilient order synchronization
pages.body:
# Requirement

Order synchronization must remain asynchronous and must never block the primary business transaction. A failed delivery may be retried at most five times.

## Acceptance criteria

After the fifth failed attempt the message is moved to the dead-letter queue and an operational alert is emitted.

pages.title: Exponential backoff decision
pages.body:
# Decision

Retries are executed by the asynchronous worker using exponential backoff with jitter. Retry behavior must not be implemented inside the remote API client.

## Rationale

Jitter reduces synchronized retry storms after a downstream outage while preserving the maximum-attempt requirement.

pages.title: Order synchronization worker
pages.body:
# Current implementation

The OrderSyncWorker consumes queued order events and sends them to the ERP adapter. The current implementation uses a fixed retry interval of five seconds and records the final failure before sending the event to the dead-letter queue.

## Dependencies

The worker depends on the event queue, ERP adapter, monitoring service and dead-letter processor.

pages.title: Retry policy verification
pages.body:
# Retry tests

The test suite verifies that a transient ERP failure is retried, that no more than five delivery attempts occur and that the final failed message reaches the dead-letter queue.

## Regression coverage

The primary transaction remains non-blocking while retries are pending.

pages.title: ERP outage retry storm incident
pages.body:
# Incident

During an ERP outage many workers retried at the same fixed interval. The synchronized retries caused a thundering-herd load spike as soon as the ERP became reachable.

## Lesson learned

Backoff should include jitter so workers do not retry simultaneously.

pages.title: Idempotent processing
pages.body:
# Idempotency

Idempotent processing prevents the same business event from producing duplicate side effects when a delivery is repeated.

## Pattern

Persist an idempotency key and reject or safely replay duplicate requests.

pages.title: Orders API
pages.body:
# Create order

POST /orders accepts an Idempotency-Key header so callers can safely retry a request without creating duplicate orders.

## Errors

A 409 response indicates a conflicting request state rather than a transient delivery failure.

pages.title: Service authentication decision
pages.body:
# Decision

Service-to-service calls use short-lived OAuth credentials. Static shared passwords are not permitted.

## Scope

The rule applies to internal APIs and asynchronous workers calling protected services.

pages.title: Operational reporting
pages.body:
# Reporting

Operational dashboards aggregate successful and failed processing counts by day and region.

pages.title: REQ-204 invoice API throttling
pages.body:
# REQ-204

The endpoint /v2/invoices must accept at most 120 write requests per minute for each tenant.

## Error contract

When the tenant limit is exceeded the API returns HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header.

pages.title: Processo di approvazione fatture
pages.body:
# Processo attuale

Le fatture con importo superiore a 10.000 euro richiedono l'approvazione di un responsabile finanziario prima della contabilizzazione.

## Eccezioni

Le note di credito seguono un flusso separato e non utilizzano questa soglia.

pages.title: Warehouse allocation policy
pages.body:
# Allocation rule

An order is allocated to the closest eligible warehouse that has sufficient available stock.

## Constraint

A warehouse under maintenance is never considered eligible even when stock is available.

pages.title: Invoice batch processing decision
pages.body:
# Decision

Nightly invoice exports are processed in batches and are not subject to the interactive API write-rate limit.

## Rationale

Batch exports have an independent capacity envelope and retry policy.
